```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Dadkhah_2022_busulfan"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Dadkhah_2022_busulfan"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics14061145> (open access)

Dadkhah 2022 fitted busulfan and its metabolite sulfolane together in adults
with myelofibrosis who received reduced-intensity busulfan/fludarabine
conditioning before allogeneic stem cell transplantation. Each analyte has one
compartment. A fixed fraction (MF = 7.04%) of total busulfan clearance forms
sulfolane (Figure 1). Total body weight scales busulfan volume, and a GSTA1
promoter SNP (-52G>A, rs3957356) raises sulfolane clearance. Busulfan
clearance carries inter-occasion variability.

# Population

Thirty-seven patients with myelofibrosis (19 female, 18 male) were treated at
the University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf. Thirty were enrolled
prospectively between November 2018 and June 2020 and seven retrospectively
from October 2016 to October 2017 (Section 2.1 and Section 3.1). Median age was
60 years (IQR 53.5-65.5) and median total body weight 75 kg (IQR 64.05-88.25)
(Table 1). Eighteen patients had primary myelofibrosis, 9 post-essential
thrombocythaemia and 10 post-polycythaemia vera myelofibrosis. The GSTA1
-52G>A SNP was found in 28 patients (75.7%) and a GSTM1 deletion in 19.

Thirty patients (81%) received ten 0.8 mg/kg doses of busulfan, each a 2 h
infusion every 6 h (Q6H). Seven (19%) received three 3.2 mg/kg doses as 3 h
infusions every 24 h (Q24H), with the later doses adjusted where needed to a
cumulative AUC (cAUC) of 50 mg x h/L (Section 2.2). The dataset held 282 busulfan
and 241 sulfolane concentrations. Sulfolane was measured only in the
prospective patients, and 70 sulfolane samples were below the 0.04 mg/L limit
of quantification.

The same information is available programmatically:

```{r population}
pop <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Dadkhah_2022_busulfan"))$population
str(pop, max.level = 1)
```

# Source trace

Each `ini()` entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Dadkhah_2022_busulfan.R`
carries its source as an in-file comment. The table below collects them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Structure | 1-cmt busulfan, 1-cmt sulfolane, IV infusion | Section 3.2; Figure 1 |
| Formation `fm * kel * central` | sulfolane formed from total CLBu | Figure 1 arrow 'CLBu x MF' and caption |
| `lcl` (CLBu) | 16.3 L/h | Table 2 (RSE 3.6%); Section 3.3 |
| `lvc` (VBu, 75 kg) | 61.5 L | Table 2 (RSE 2%) |
| `e_wt_vc` | 0.854 | Table 2 'COV_V Bu _TBW'; equation (1) `VBu = VBu-typ * (TBW/75)^0.854` |
| `fm` (MF) | 0.0704 | Table 2 (RSE 28.6%) |
| `lcl_sulfolane` (CLSu, non-carrier) | 1.61 L/h | Table 2 (RSE 37%) |
| `lvc_sulfolane` (VSu) | 48.8 L | Table 2 (RSE 35.2%) |
| `e_gsta1_cl_sulfolane` | 1.43 | Table 2 'COV_CL Su _GSTA1'; equation (2) `CLSu = CLSu-typ * e^1.43` for GSTA1 |
| `etalcl` | 0.045171 | Table 2 'IIV CL Bu' 21.5% CV; `log(1 + CV^2)` per the Table 2 footnote |
| `etalvc` | 0.009950 | Table 2 'IIV V Bu' 10% CV |
| `etalcl_sulfolane` | 0.820843 | Table 2 'IIV CL Su' 112.8% CV |
| `etalvc_sulfolane` | 0.471361 | Table 2 'IIV V Su' 77.6% CV |
| `etaiov_cl_1..3` | 0.005759 each | Table 2 'IOV CL Bu' 7.6% CV; occasions defined in Section 3.2 |
| `propSd` | 0.071 | Table 2 'Prop. sigma Bu' 7.1% |
| `propSd_sulfolane` | 0.362 | Table 2 'Prop. sigma Su' 36.2% |

# Typical values against the abstract

The abstract quotes the typical parameters per kilogram for a 75 kg patient:
busulfan CL 0.217 L/h/kg and V 0.82 L/kg, sulfolane CL 0.021 L/h/kg and V
0.65 L/kg. These come from the same Table 2 estimates, so only rounding
separates them.

```{r typical-values}
mod <- readModelDb("Dadkhah_2022_busulfan")

ev_typ <- data.frame(
  id = 1L, time = 0, evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L,
  WT = 75, SNP_GSTA1_RS3957356 = 0L, OCC = 1L
)
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = ev_typ, useLinCmt = FALSE) |>
  as.data.frame()

typ_tab <- tibble::tibble(
  parameter = c("Busulfan CL (L/h/kg)", "Busulfan V (L/kg)", "Sulfolane CL (L/h/kg)", "Sulfolane V (L/kg)"),
  model = c(typ$cl, typ$vc, typ$cl_sulfolane, typ$vc_sulfolane) / 75,
  abstract = c(0.217, 0.82, 0.021, 0.65)
)
typ_tab |>
  dplyr::rename("Parameter" = parameter, "Model" = model, "Abstract" = abstract) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4, caption = "Typical values for a 75 kg GSTA1 SNP non-carrier.")

# Same estimates on both sides; the abstract rounds to two or three digits.
stopifnot(max(abs(typ_tab$model - typ_tab$abstract) / typ_tab$abstract) < 0.03)
```

# Virtual cohort

The individual data are not public. Body weight is drawn log-normally with the
Table 1 median (75 kg) and a spread matching its interquartile range
(64.05-88.25 kg, so `sdlog = log(88.25 / 64.05) / 1.349 = 0.238`), truncated
to 40-150 kg. Each subject carries the GSTA1 SNP with probability 0.757.

Occasions follow Section 3.2: each sampled administration opens a new occasion.
Q6H patients were sampled after the first, fifth and ninth infusions, so
doses 1-4 are occasion 1, doses 5-8 occasion 2 and doses 9-10 occasion 3. Q24H
patients were sampled after the first infusion only, so all three of their
doses are occasion 1.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20220527)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20220527)

n_q6h <- 200L
n_q24h <- 200L

draw_wt <- function(n) {
  wt <- exp(rnorm(n, log(75), log(88.25 / 64.05) / 1.349))
  pmin(pmax(wt, 40), 150)
}

subj_q6h <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_q6h),
  regimen = "Q6H",
  WT = draw_wt(n_q6h),
  SNP_GSTA1_RS3957356 = rbinom(n_q6h, 1, 0.757)
)
subj_q24h <- tibble::tibble(
  id = n_q6h + seq_len(n_q24h),
  regimen = "Q24H",
  WT = draw_wt(n_q24h),
  SNP_GSTA1_RS3957356 = rbinom(n_q24h, 1, 0.757)
)

# Observation rows sit on the busulfan state with dvid = 1; rxode2 returns
# both Cc and Cc_sulfolane as columns at every observation time.
make_events <- function(subj, dose_times, dose_mgkg, inf_dur, obs_times, occ_breaks) {
  doses <- tidyr::crossing(subj, time = dose_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 1L, amt = dose_mgkg * WT, rate = amt / inf_dur, dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs <- tidyr::crossing(subj, time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0, dvid = 1L)
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      cmt = "central",
      OCC = findInterval(time, occ_breaks)
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    as.data.frame()
}

grid_q6h <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 84, by = 0.25), 2.08, 48 + 2.08)))
ev_q6h <- make_events(
  subj_q6h,
  dose_times = seq(0, 54, by = 6), dose_mgkg = 0.8, inf_dur = 2,
  obs_times = grid_q6h, occ_breaks = c(0, 24, 48)
)
# Q24H: first dose only (the later doses depend on the TDM result, below).
ev_q24h <- make_events(
  subj_q24h,
  dose_times = 0, dose_mgkg = 3.2, inf_dur = 3,
  obs_times = seq(0, 36, by = 0.25), occ_breaks = 0
)
stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(ev_q6h[, c("id", "time", "evid")]),
  setequal(unique(ev_q6h$OCC), 1:3),
  all(ev_q24h$OCC == 1L)
)
summary(subj_q6h$WT)
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim_q6h <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = ev_q6h, keep = c("regimen", "WT", "SNP_GSTA1_RS3957356"), useLinCmt = FALSE
) |>
  as.data.frame()
sim_q24h <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = ev_q24h, keep = c("regimen", "WT", "SNP_GSTA1_RS3957356"), useLinCmt = FALSE
) |>
  as.data.frame()
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim_q6h$Cc), !anyNA(sim_q6h$Cc_sulfolane), !anyNA(sim_q24h$Cc))
```

# Replicate published results

## Concentration-time profiles (Figure 3)

Figure 3 of the paper is a prediction-corrected VPC for the Q6H patients,
plotted against time after the first and ninth doses. The panels below show
the 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles of the simulated Q6H concentrations,
including residual error, over the whole 10-dose course. The grey line in the
sulfolane panel marks the 0.04 mg/L LLOQ. Residual error is added to each
analyte by hand because the observation rows carry the busulfan endpoint.

```{r figure-3}
vpc <- sim_q6h |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Busulfan = Cc * (1 + 0.071 * rnorm(dplyr::n())),
    Sulfolane = Cc_sulfolane * (1 + 0.362 * rnorm(dplyr::n()))
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Busulfan, Sulfolane) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Busulfan, Sulfolane), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::group_by(analyte, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(conc, 0.05), Q50 = quantile(conc, 0.50), Q95 = quantile(conc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc, aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(
    data = data.frame(analyte = "Sulfolane", y = 0.04), aes(yintercept = y),
    colour = "grey50"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~analyte, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Time since first dose (h)",
    y = "Concentration (mg/L)",
    caption = "Simulated Q6H 5th-50th-95th percentiles; compare with Figure 3 of Dadkhah 2022."
  )
```

Sulfolane accumulates over the course because its typical half-life
(`log(2) * 48.8 / 1.61` = 21 h in non-carriers, 5 h in carriers) is long
against the 6 h dosing interval.

## Sulfolane below the limit of quantification

Section 3.1 reports 70 of 241 sulfolane samples (29%) below 0.04 mg/L. Here the
simulated Q6H concentrations, with residual error, are read at the protocol
sampling times: 2.08, 3, 4 and 5.5 h after the first and ninth infusions and
5.5 h after the fifth (Section 2.2).

```{r blq}
samp_times <- c(2.08, 3, 4, 5.5, 24 + 5.5, 48 + c(2.08, 3, 4, 5.5))
blq <- sim_q6h |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% samp_times) |>
  dplyr::mutate(obs = Cc_sulfolane * (1 + 0.362 * rnorm(dplyr::n())), blq = obs < 0.04)

blq_by_time <- blq |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(pct_blq = 100 * mean(blq), .groups = "drop")
blq_by_time |>
  dplyr::rename("Time since first dose (h)" = time, "Simulated BLQ (%)" = pct_blq) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Share of simulated sulfolane samples below 0.04 mg/L.")
overall_blq <- 100 * mean(blq$blq)
overall_blq
```

Overall `r round(overall_blq)`% of the simulated samples are below the LLOQ,
against 29% observed. Most come from the first dosing day, before sulfolane
has accumulated, as in the lower panel of Figure 3B. The observed share also
includes the Q24H patients' samples, and the paper does not give the sample
count per time point, so this check is reported but not gated.

## Busulfan cumulative AUC (Section 3.1)

Section 3.1 reports a median busulfan cAUC of 36.06 mg x h/L (range
25.67-61.85) over all 37 patients. PKNCA computes the Q6H cAUC from the dense
simulated profile from 0 to 84 h (30 h after the last infusion). For the Q24H arm, PKNCA computes the first-dose AUC to infinity,
and the second and third doses are then set so that the cAUC reaches
50 mg x h/L (Section 2.2). Because Q24H patients have a single occasion and the
model is linear, the adjusted cAUC is exactly 50 by construction.

```{r pknca-cauc}
nca_conc <- dplyr::bind_rows(sim_q6h, sim_q24h) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, regimen, time, Cc)
nca_dose <- dplyr::bind_rows(ev_q6h, ev_q24h) |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1L) |>
  dplyr::select(id, regimen, time, amt)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | regimen + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | regimen + id)
# Q6H: the whole course (cAUC), the three occasion windows, and the first
# dosing interval. Q24H: first dose to infinity and its first 24 h.
intervals <- data.frame(
  regimen = c("Q6H", "Q6H", "Q6H", "Q6H", "Q6H", "Q24H", "Q24H"),
  start = c(0, 0, 24, 48, 0, 0, 0),
  end = c(84, 24, 48, 84, 6, Inf, 24),
  auclast = c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE),
  aucinf.obs = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE),
  cmax = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE),
  tmax = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  conc_obj, dose_obj,
  intervals = intervals,
  options = list(auc.method = "lin up/log down")
))
nca_df <- as.data.frame(nca_res)
summary(nca_res)
```

The PKNCA AUCs are checked against mass balance. Busulfan is eliminated only
through CL, so over the whole course the total dose equals
`sum(CL_k * AUC_k)`, where `AUC_k` is the AUC within occasion k's time window
and `CL_k` is that occasion's clearance. (A simpler `sum(dose / CL)` is not
exact here: drug still in the body when a new occasion opens is cleared at
the new occasion's clearance.) The busulfan still in the body at 84 h is added
to the eliminated amount, since heavy subjects with low clearance have a
half-life of several hours. The two sides share the drawn parameters, so only
the trapezoidal error separates them.

```{r cauc-closed-form}
cl_occ <- sim_q6h |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, OCC, cl)
q6h_auc <- nca_df |>
  dplyr::filter(regimen == "Q6H", PPTESTCD == "auclast")
mass_balance <- q6h_auc |>
  dplyr::filter(end != 84 | start != 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(OCC = findInterval(start, c(0, 24, 48))) |>
  dplyr::left_join(cl_occ, by = c("id", "OCC")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(eliminated = sum(cl * PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    sim_q6h |>
      dplyr::filter(time == 84) |>
      dplyr::select(id, remaining = central),
    by = "id"
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    ev_q6h |>
      dplyr::filter(evid == 1L) |>
      dplyr::group_by(id) |>
      dplyr::summarise(total_dose = sum(amt), .groups = "drop"),
    by = "id"
  )

cauc_q6h <- q6h_auc |>
  dplyr::filter(start == 0, end == 84) |>
  dplyr::select(id, cauc = PPORRES)
stopifnot(
  nrow(cauc_q6h) == n_q6h,
  nrow(mass_balance) == n_q6h,
  max(abs((mass_balance$eliminated + mass_balance$remaining) / mass_balance$total_dose - 1)) < 0.01
)

auc1_q24h <- nca_df |>
  dplyr::filter(regimen == "Q24H", PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  dplyr::select(id, auc1 = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::distinct(sim_q24h, id, cl), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(subj_q24h, id, WT), by = "id")
stopifnot(max(abs(auc1_q24h$auc1 / (3.2 * auc1_q24h$WT / auc1_q24h$cl) - 1)) < 0.01)

# Doses 2 and 3 share the remaining exposure: (50 - AUC1) * CL each half.
q24h_adj <- auc1_q24h |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dose23_mgkg = (50 - auc1) * cl / 2 / WT,
    cauc = auc1 + 2 * dose23_mgkg * WT / cl
  )
summary(q24h_adj$dose23_mgkg)
```

The adjusted Q24H doses (median `r round(median(q24h_adj$dose23_mgkg), 2)`
mg/kg) sit a little above the 3.2 mg/kg starting dose, as expected for a
50 mg x h/L target.

The published median covers all 37 patients, 30 of them on Q6H. The table
gives the simulated Q6H arm and, for reference, the two arms pooled in the
study's 30:7 ratio (all 200 Q6H subjects plus the first 47 Q24H subjects).

```{r cauc-compare}
cauc_pool <- c(cauc_q6h$cauc, head(q24h_adj$cauc, round(n_q6h * 7 / 30)))
cauc_tab <- tibble::tibble(
  statistic = c("Median", "Minimum", "Maximum"),
  q6h = c(median(cauc_q6h$cauc), min(cauc_q6h$cauc), max(cauc_q6h$cauc)),
  pooled = c(median(cauc_pool), min(cauc_pool), max(cauc_pool)),
  published = c(36.06, 25.67, 61.85)
)
cauc_tab |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "cAUC (mg*h/L)" = statistic, "Simulated Q6H" = q6h,
    "Simulated Q6H + Q24H (30:7)" = pooled, "Published, all 37 (Section 3.1)" = published
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Busulfan cumulative AUC.")

# Centre of the Q6H distribution: a mis-transcribed CL, dose or unit would
# move the median by tens of percent.
stopifnot(abs(median(cauc_q6h$cauc) / 36.06 - 1) < 0.1)
```

The simulated Q6H median is within 6% of the published median. The pooled
median runs higher, for two reasons. The simulated Q24H subjects all reach
exactly 50 mg x h/L, because their doses are adjusted using their true
clearance. The simulated spread is also wider than the observed one: cAUC
scales with weight / CL, the model has no weight effect on busulfan
clearance, and so the weight spread and the 21.5% CV IIV on clearance add up.
The 37 patients span 25.7-61.9 mg x h/L, a 2.4-fold range, while 200 simulated
subjects span `r round(max(cauc_q6h$cauc) / min(cauc_q6h$cauc), 1)`-fold. Neither the pooled median nor the range is
gated.

## Individual busulfan clearance after the first and ninth doses

Section 3.1 gives the median individual busulfan clearance as 17.16 L/h after
the first dose (range 10.55-22.36) and 16.47 L/h after the ninth (range
10.05-19.27), from the post hoc estimates. The simulated Q6H clearances on
occasions 1 and 3 are summarised below.

```{r cl-occasions}
cl_tab <- cl_occ |>
  dplyr::filter(OCC %in% c(1L, 3L)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(OCC) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median = median(cl), q05 = quantile(cl, 0.05), q95 = quantile(cl, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(published_median = c(17.16, 16.47))
cl_tab |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Occasion" = OCC, "Median (L/h)" = median, "5th pct" = q05, "95th pct" = q95,
    "Published median (L/h)" = published_median
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Simulated busulfan clearance by occasion (Q6H).")
stopifnot(all(abs(cl_tab$median / cl_tab$published_median - 1) < 0.1))
```

The model has no time trend in clearance, so the simulated medians on the two
occasions agree. The small drop the paper reports between doses 1 and 9 is a
feature of the 37 patients' post hoc estimates and is within the 7.6% IOV.

## Sulfolane formation: mass balance

With formation `MF * CLBu * Cc` and first-order sulfolane elimination, a
single busulfan dose D gives a sulfolane AUC to infinity of `MF * D / CLSu`.
PKNCA is run on a typical-value single 60 mg dose for a GSTA1 non-carrier and
a carrier, followed for 200 h.

```{r mass-balance}
ev_mb <- tidyr::crossing(
  tibble::tibble(id = 1:2, SNP_GSTA1_RS3957356 = c(0L, 1L)),
  time = c(0, seq(0.25, 200, by = 0.25))
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    evid = ifelse(time == 0, 1L, 0L), amt = ifelse(time == 0, 60, 0),
    rate = ifelse(time == 0, 30, 0), dvid = ifelse(time == 0, NA_integer_, 1L),
    cmt = "central", WT = 75, OCC = 1L
  )
# Observation at time 0 for the PKNCA pre-dose record
ev_mb <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  ev_mb,
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::filter(ev_mb, time == 0), evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0, dvid = 1L)
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
  as.data.frame()

sim_mb <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
  events = ev_mb, keep = "SNP_GSTA1_RS3957356", useLinCmt = FALSE,
  atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(genotype = ifelse(SNP_GSTA1_RS3957356 == 1, "carrier", "non-carrier"))

mb_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(
  dplyr::filter(sim_mb, !is.na(Cc_sulfolane)),
  Cc_sulfolane ~ time | genotype + id
)
mb_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::filter(ev_mb, evid == 1L),
    genotype = ifelse(SNP_GSTA1_RS3957356 == 1, "carrier", "non-carrier")
  ),
  amt ~ time | genotype + id
)
mb_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  mb_conc, mb_dose,
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
))
mb <- as.data.frame(mb_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  dplyr::select(genotype, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    cl_su = 1.61 * ifelse(genotype == "carrier", exp(1.43), 1),
    auc_closed = 0.0704 * 60 / cl_su,
    thalf_closed = log(2) * 48.8 / cl_su
  )
mb |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "GSTA1 SNP" = genotype, "AUCinf PKNCA (mg*h/L)" = aucinf.obs,
    "AUCinf closed form" = auc_closed, "t1/2 PKNCA (h)" = half.life,
    "t1/2 closed form (h)" = thalf_closed, "CLSu (L/h)" = cl_su
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Sulfolane exposure after a single 60 mg busulfan dose, typical values.")

# Same parameters on both sides: only the trapezoidal error separates them.
stopifnot(
  max(abs(mb$aucinf.obs / mb$auc_closed - 1)) < 0.01,
  max(abs(mb$half.life / mb$thalf_closed - 1)) < 0.01
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Direction of the GSTA1 effect.** Equation (2) multiplies sulfolane
  clearance by exp(1.43) 'for GSTA1' and leaves it unchanged 'for
  non-GSTA1'. With the GSTA1 SNP coded 0/1 (Section 2.5) and 75.7% of patients
  carrying it (Table 1), the model reads 'for GSTA1' as SNP present
  (`SNP_GSTA1_RS3957356 = 1`). The Table 2 CLSu of 1.61 L/h is then the
  non-carrier value, and carriers clear sulfolane 4.18-fold faster. The
  Discussion itself calls this direction counterintuitive. The simulated
  sulfolane BLQ fraction is similar under either reading, so it cannot settle
  the question.
- **Metabolic fraction on a mass basis.** The paper describes no molar
  conversion. Busulfan doses are in mg and both analytes are reported in mg/L
  (LLOQ 0.04 mg/L), so MF is applied to busulfan mass. Read this way, 0.0704
  is a mass ratio: in moles it corresponds to 0.0704 x 246.30 / 120.17 = 14.4%
  of busulfan becoming sulfolane. Had the authors modelled in molar amounts,
  the sulfolane concentrations simulated here would be about 2-fold too high.
- **Correlated residual errors not carried.** The authors linked the
  busulfan and sulfolane proportional errors through a NONMEM L2 sigma block
  (correlation 11.8%, Section 3.2). nlmixr2 has no correlated residual-error
  syntax, so the two errors are independent here. This affects only
  simulations with residual error and only the joint distribution of paired
  samples.
- **Residual-error scale.** Table 2 reports the proportional errors as CV%.
  They are taken directly as proportional SDs (0.071 and 0.362).
- **IIV scale.** Table 2 converts each omega to %CV with
  `sqrt(exp(OMEGA) - 1)`, so the variances are `log(1 + CV^2)`.
- **Occasions.** Section 3.2 defines a new occasion at each administration
  followed by sampling. For the Q6H protocol this gives three occasions
  (doses 1-4, 5-8 and 9-10). Q24H patients have one. Occasion 2 is
  defined by a trough sample only. The single IOV variance in Table 2 is used
  for all three occasions.
- **Below-LLOQ data.** The authors kept BLQ sulfolane samples in the fit and
  let the error model absorb them (Section 3.2). This affects estimation only,
  not simulation.
- **Virtual cohort.** Body weight is log-normal from the Table 1 median and
  IQR. The Q24H dose adjustment uses each subject's simulated clearance
  directly, which stands in for the clinical TDM. The paper gives only the
  cAUC target of 50 mg x h/L and not the adjustment algorithm.
- **Covariates screened but not retained** (JAK2 mutation, GSTM1 deletion,
  De Ritis ratio, alkaline phosphatase, bilirubin) are listed in the model's
  `covariatesDataExcluded` metadata.
- No correction notice for the article was found as of 2026-10-01.
